failure_summary.description: Answers were too broad, too narrow, or used a title spelling that did not match the expected canonical form.
The response missed the requested referent or chose a less directly supported candidate despite the clue and context.
A bare entity prompt was answered with a definition rather than the missing attribute implied by context.

patch.reasoning: Clarify that parody-title guidance applies only when a title is requested, add a procedure for bare-entity prompts, and distinguish complete canonical titles from descriptive clue modifiers. The direct-evidence selection failures already fall under existing rules, so they do not warrant a duplicate edit.

edits.target: When a question describes a title as changed, adapted, or parodied, distinguish the original title from the altered title. Use the wording to determine which is requested: a reference to the original work or an author's title asks for the original; a question asking what the adaptation, parody, or short was called asks for the altered title. Do not mistake the described change for the requested answer.
edits.content: When a question describes a title as changed, adapted, or parodied, distinguish the original title from the altered title. Use the wording to determine which is requested: a reference to the original work or an author's title asks for the original; a question asking what the adaptation, parody, or short was called asks for the altered title. Apply this rule only when the requested answer is a title: if the question asks which person, character, or entity was parodied, give that referent rather than the parody's title.

### Bare entity prompts
- When the prompt is only an entity name, use the task framing and context to infer the missing attribute, then return that attribute rather than an encyclopedia-style definition. Base the inference on a directly supported relation in the context; if no relation can be inferred, do not invent one.

### Canonical titles and labels
- For a named work, event, or concept, retain the full conventional title or label rather than shortening it to one of its components. Omit descriptive modifiers that are not part of the canonical name, and use the established spelling and spacing.
